chunks: "I'd draw four little pictures. Time domain at the transmitter: without preemphasis a plain NRZ waveform, levels at plus and minus full swing, flat between transitions.
With de-emphasis it looks the same on the first bit after every transition, full height, but if the data stays the same the next bits sit lower, at about half height for a 6 decibels setting.
The result is a waveform with a 'shoulder' after each edge. Time domain at the receiver: the lossy channel rounds everything.
Without preemphasis a single isolated bit barely reaches the threshold because it's too short, while a run of ones reaches full height, so the eye height is set by the worst isolated bit.
With de-emphasis the run of ones is lower and the single bit is relatively higher, so all the received levels are closer to uniform and the eye is bigger.
Frequency domain: the NRZ spectrum is a sinc-squared lobe, flat near DC, falling toward the first null at the bit rate.
The preemphasis filter is a high-pass shelf, down 6 decibels at DC and 0 decibels around the Nyquist frequency.
So the transmitted spectrum has its low-frequency part pushed down and its high end relatively raised.
After the channel, whose response falls with frequency, the product is flatter without preemphasis being more tilted."
